names.official: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

summary: Papua New Guinea gives a visa on arrival to a short list of countries — including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific. ICSA's eVisa portal lists the passports eligible for a 60-day Easy Visitor Permit applied for online in advance (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee), among them the US, New Zealand, the EU states and most of the visa-on-arrival countries. Other nationalities apply for a visitor visa on the paper form before travel. Melanesian Spearhead Group neighbors get a 30-day visa on arrival.

currencyLimits.text: Travellers carrying currency or valuables worth PGK 20,000 or more must declare them on a Cross-Border Movement of Currency and Valuables (CMCV) form, available at all customs entry and exit points. Failing to declare, or giving false information, can bring a fine of up to PGK 50,000 or five years' imprisonment.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to enter Papua New Guinea with many fruits, vegetables and animal products because of local quarantine controls, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to duty.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high risk of serious crime in Port Moresby, Lae and Mount Hagen, that carjacking and other vehicle crime are common, and that walking after dark is particularly dangerous in urban centres. It advises against all but essential travel to Hela and Southern Highlands provinces and to Enga (except Wabag District) because of tribal fighting.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high risk of serious crime in Port Moresby, Lae and Mount Hagen, that walking after dark is particularly dangerous in urban centres, and that criminals target people using banks and ATMs. It advises not travelling alone or at night, and keeping car doors locked and windows up.

If your passport is on the eVisa portal's Easy Visitor Permit list, which includes the US, New Zealand, the EU states and most visa-on-arrival countries, you can apply for the permit through the official eVisa portal; ICSA's guide gives a turnaround of 10 working days when all requirements are met. Everyone else applies for a visitor visa before flying.

Canada's travel health advice says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas of Papua New Guinea, and dengue is also a risk. It advises consulting a travel health clinic about antimalarials, ideally 6 weeks before travel, and protecting yourself from mosquito bites at all times.
The UK Foreign Office says delays and cancellations of international and domestic flights often happen, and advises checking with your airline before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, every foreign visitor needs a visa. Citizens of the countries on ICSA's visa-on-arrival list, including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific, can get one on arrival, and Fijian, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu citizens get a 30-day visa on arrival. ICSA's eVisa portal lists the passports eligible for the 60-day Easy Visitor Permit, applied for online in advance (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee), among them the US, New Zealand and the EU states; other nationalities, including Australians, apply for a visitor visa before travel.

faq.question: How do I apply for the PNG tourist eVisa?
faq.answer: ICSA's Visitor Visa page opens the eVisa portal to citizens of the countries on its visa-on-arrival list. For the Easy Visitor Permit, ICSA's guide asks for a request letter, a copy of your passport bio page, and your travel itinerary with a confirmed onward or return ticket and a guarantee that you are financially secure; the turnaround is 10 working days when all requirements are met. The eVisa portal's own Easy Visitor Permit page lists the eligible passports, among them the US, New Zealand and the EU states; other nationalities use the paper visitor-visa form.

faq.question: Is there a visa on arrival in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, for the countries on the visa-on-arrival list published by the Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority. The list includes the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and most Pacific Island states; mainland New Zealand, France and the United States are not eligible. Chinese ordinary passport holders qualify only in an organised tour group.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: The 60-day Easy Visitor Permit is a single-entry stay of 60 days from arrival, and ICSA says a visitor visa is in most circumstances a single-entry stay of 60 days. Depending on the visa, ICSA says you may be able to extend your stay without leaving the country.

faq.question: Is Papua New Guinea safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high risk of serious crime in Port Moresby, Lae and Mount Hagen and that walking after dark is particularly dangerous in urban centres, and it advises against all but essential travel to Hela and Southern Highlands provinces and to Enga (except Wabag District) because of tribal fighting.

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited through the airport of, a yellow fever risk country. No official source we could read lists any other compulsory vaccination. Canada's travel health advice recommends hepatitis A vaccination for all travellers and up-to-date routine vaccines, and says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas, so ask a travel health clinic about antimalarials.
